attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the carve-out for initial customers and the 'we haven't seen it' framing. It reports what the speaker has observed, with no threshold for what counts as a moat.

contract.note: The contract rightly finds no test: 'moat' has no stated durability or threshold, and the claim is about what the speaker has seen. Scoring it would mean inventing a market test.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own 2023 disclosure about its Microsoft distribution deals. It shows a possible advantage but cannot settle whether that is a moat. Dated before the post.

reviews.rationale: This is a qualified statement about what the speaker has seen, using 'moat' with no stated threshold or durability. No fair support or contradiction test exists without adding criteria he did not give. The Microsoft partnership is only context.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion, made while criticising Altman. The quoted 'we're making AGI' is Altman's, but the claim scored here is Marcus's own description of the field.

semantics.note: The revision restores 'struggled', 'entire field' and 'for decades'. It is a historical observation running up to the post date.

contract.note: The plain reading (major general problems stayed unsolved, while some progress happened) is the ordinary meaning of 'struggled to solve'. It is not stretched either way.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own March 2023 disclosure, an admission against its interest, that GPT-4 hallucinates and makes reasoning errors. It also reports progress, which fits 'struggled' rather than 'no progress'.
Feb 2024 preprint: only about 12% of GPT-4's plans were executable in autonomous mode. Shows unresolved planning weaknesses before the post.
Jan 2024 survey: hallucination is still a major obstacle to deployment despite many mitigation techniques.
Independent Stanford AI Index: $25.2B of generative-AI investment in 2023 supports 'massively well-capitalized'. Published before the post.
McCarthy's 1984 lecture on brittleness and unsolved common-sense reasoning supports the decades-long history for reasoning and reliability, though not for modern hallucination.

reviews.rationale: All the evidence is dated before the post. It shows persistent weaknesses in reliability, reasoning, planning and hallucination despite active work and heavy investment. McCarthy shows the decades-long history for reasoning and brittleness. The progress OpenAI reports fits 'struggled'. Supported on the plain reading.
